summary: Phase 7 can falsely report successful persistence and its advertised overwrite recovery path deletes the recovery artifact.

findings.title: Append verification can report success after a failed write
findings.description: The append path never checks whether the append command actually succeeded, and the read-back only proves that the current last line has a `schema_version`. If `echo ... >> "$INDEX_FILE"` fails on an existing index because of quota, permissions changes, NFS/transient I/O, or shell redirection failure, `tail -1` can still read the previous valid entry and the flow will print success even though the new entry was never persisted. That creates a false-success checkpoint for the storage layer and makes reruns/recovery unreliable because the user believes the analysis is indexed when it is not.
findings.recommendation: Check the append command exit status before validation, then validate that the last parsed line matches the new entry's exact `id` and `dedup_key` rather than only checking `.schema_version`; preferably write via temp file plus atomic rename or use `flock` around dedup+append.

findings.title: Overwrite recovery file is deleted on mv failure
findings.description: The overwrite failure branch promises that the temp file is preserved for manual recovery, but the cleanup trap is still active when `mv` fails and `exit 1` runs. In that failure path the trap removes `$TEMP_FILE`, so the new combined index that was supposed to be recoverable is deleted. This turns a partial-failure recovery path into a dead end and gives the operator incorrect recovery instructions at exactly the point where the index update failed.
findings.recommendation: Disable or adjust the cleanup trap before the `mv` failure handler if the temp file should be preserved, e.g. `mv ... || { trap - EXIT; echo ...; exit 1; }`, or change the message and recovery procedure to reflect that the temp file is intentionally removed.

next_steps: Fix the write verification to prove the new entry persisted, not just that the file remains parseable.
Correct the overwrite failure trap/message so manual recovery is possible and truthful.
